sections.title: InterContinental New Orleans
sections.intro: The 2027 MISMO Winter Summit will be held at the InterContinental New Orleans, in the heart of the Central Business District on St Charles Avenue.

cards.name: Getting Here
cards.text: Louis Armstrong New Orleans International (MSY) is about 12 miles from the hotel. Taxis charge a flat $36 for one or two passengers, or $15 per person for three or more. The RTA Airport Express (Route 202) runs downtown to Poydras Street for $1.25.

cards.name: Getting Around
cards.text:
A St. Charles Streetcar stop is directly across from the hotel — $1.25 a ride, running 24 hours. The French Quarter is about a five-minute walk. Valet parking is available at the hotel; there is no on-site self parking.

Use the booking link below to get the group rate.

cards.name: What to Expect in January
cards.text: January averages a high of 63°F and a low of 46°F, and it is one of the wetter months — pack a rain jacket. Check-in is 4:00 PM and check-out is 11:00 AM.

roomBlock.title: Reserve at the InterContinental New Orleans
roomBlock.text: Book through the MISMO group link below to receive the discounted rate for January 11–14, 2027. The cut-off date is Monday, December 14, 2026. Rooms are released once the block is full or the cut-off date passes, whichever comes first.

sections.title: Dining Within Walking Distance
sections.intro: The InterContinental sits in the Central Business District, a few blocks from some of the best cooking in the country.

cards.name: Trenasse
cards.text: Louisiana seafood and a raw oyster bar on the ground floor of the InterContinental. The easy answer when sessions run late.

cards.name: Luke
cards.text: A German-Alsatian brasserie with a long oyster happy hour. Big tables, good for groups.

cards.name: Mother’s Restaurant
cards.text: A New Orleans institution since 1938. Po’boys, red beans and rice, and a line worth standing in.

cards.name: Herbsaint
cards.text: Donald Link’s flagship and a James Beard Award winner. French-Louisiana cooking in a room built for a long dinner.

cards.name: Compère Lapin
cards.text: Chef Nina Compton’s Caribbean-Creole cooking in the Old No. 77 Hotel. One of the most celebrated kitchens in the city.

cards.name: Pêche Seafood Grill
cards.text: Whole fish over hardwood coals. Named the James Beard Best New Restaurant the year it opened.

cards.name: Cochon
cards.text: Southern Louisiana cooking built around the whole hog. Book ahead — it fills up.

cards.name: Willa Jean
cards.text: A bakery and all-day Southern kitchen. The best option near the hotel for an early breakfast meeting.

sections.note: Walking times are approximate and measured from the InterContinental at 444 St Charles Avenue.

sections.title: Things to Do Near the Hotel
sections.intro: Build a morning or an afternoon around the Summit. Everything below is walkable or a short streetcar ride away.

cards.name: The National WWII Museum
cards.text: Consistently ranked among the finest museums in the country. Give it half a day if you can.

cards.name: Ogden Museum of Southern Art
cards.text: The largest collection of Southern art anywhere, in a building worth the visit on its own.

cards.name: Contemporary Arts Center
cards.text: Rotating exhibitions, performance and film in the heart of the Warehouse Arts District.

cards.name: St. Charles Streetcar
cards.text: The oldest continuously operating streetcar line in the world. Ride it uptown past the Garden District oaks.

cards.name: The French Quarter
cards.text: Jackson Square, St. Louis Cathedral, the galleries on Royal Street and café au lait at Café du Monde.

cards.name: Frenchmen Street
cards.text: Where the locals go for live music. Three blocks of clubs, most with no cover.

cards.name: The Riverfront and Woldenberg Park
cards.text: A level walk along the Mississippi, with the Audubon Aquarium at the near end.

cards.name: Magazine Street
cards.text: Six miles of independent shops, antiques, bookstores and coffee. Catch it on the way back from the WWII Museum.
